subject: Assurance acceptance criteria + evidence sprint for Order Form
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthalpha.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: SOC 2 & pen-test language in Order Form

Stephanie / Marissa —

Thanks for sending the Order Form. Our legal team reviewed the security exhibit and had a few follow-ups before we can route to procurement:

- Can you confirm what you expect for SOC 2 evidence cadence (annual report vs. continuous access to artifacts)?
- For penetration tests: do you require Redwood to provide test results, or will HealthAlpha run a third-party test? What notice period do you expect?
- Is there a proposed window for staging access and a list of artifacts you’ll provide (log samples, configuration snapshots, audit logs)?

I’ve attached the version we received from our side — marked up with a couple of comments. Would like to align on acceptance criteria so legal and procurement can sign off.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Director, IT Security — HealthAlpha
[Attachment: security-exhibit-draft.docx]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthalpha.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: SOC 2 & pen-test language in Order Form

Samir —

Appreciate the notes. I looped in Legal (Laura) and our Assurance lead (Ben) so we can converge quickly. High-level responses and a suggested acceptance checklist below — want to be explicit so procurement has straightforward sign-off criteria.

Quick answers:
- SOC 2: we provide an annual SOC 2 Type II report (control summary + report PDF). For higher assurance we can offer a quarterly artifact package (request-based) containing scoped logs and configuration snapshots for the agreed-in-scope systems.
- Pen test: Redwood will accept customer-supplied 3P tests for recognition of findings, but we require either: (a) a mutually agreed test scope conducted by an independent lab with a redacted report shared with Redwood, or (b) Redwood-managed test with 30 days' notice.
- Staging access & artifacts: we can provide ephemeral staging credentials for scoped systems, TTL-limited to the engagement window; we’ll deliver log extracts, configuration snapshots, and role lists as a ZIP over secure transfer.

Suggested acceptance checklist (proposal):
1) SOC 2 Type II report delivered within 30 days of release each year.
2) Evidence package (on request): up to 3 artifact requests per 12 months; 10-business-day turnaround.
3) Pen test: minimum 30 days' notice for customer-run testing; no-exercise blackout periods (holiday window) to be scheduled during the mutual action plan.
4) Access: ephemeral staging credentials with max 48-hour windows; access requests require justification and signed NDA where needed.
5) Data handling: sample logs will be redacted of PII; Redwood retains right to refuse access to data containing customer PII without a court order or explicit DPA amendment.

Attachments: I added inline comments and a short redline doc highlighting the above. Can Laura propose alternate legal language if needed. If HealthAlpha agrees we can put a short Mutual Action Plan in HubSpot and schedule a 30-minute call to finalize.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Security Engagement Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_comments.pdf]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthalpha.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: SOC 2 & pen-test language in Order Form

Hi Samir / team —

Thanks for the draft and Stephanie’s checklist — that helps a lot. From a legal perspective we want to narrow the audit & inspection language so it’s operationally achievable and protective of Redwood’s multi-tenant environment. Proposed redlines summarized below (I’ll attach a tracked Word copy to the HubSpot record):

Key legal proposals (high level):
- Scope limitation: audit rights are limited to request-aligned evidence (SOC 2 report and specific artifact packages) and do not permit continuous or unfettered access to production systems.
- Sampling approach: Evidence requests will be fulfilled on a sample basis with a stated scope and limited to no more than 3 requests per rolling 12-month period, unless a material security incident occurs.
- Pen test: Customer may provide third-party pen test reports; Redwood reserves the right to corroborate findings and to require remediation before acceptance. Any customer-conducted testing affecting Redwood managed tenancy requires a mutually agreed scope, 30 days' advance notice, and a safety plan.
- Data & retention: Redwood will provide redacted artifacts for PII; Redwood’s standard evidence retention is 90 days unless otherwise contractually agreed.
- Confidentiality & sharing: All exchanged test reports and artifacts are confidential and subject to the existing NDA; HealthAlpha may not publish or share raw vulnerability findings externally without Redwood’s prior written consent.

If HealthAlpha is comfortable with the sampling cadence and the 90-day evidence retention, we can incorporate these clauses into the Order Form and circulate for signature. If you require a longer retention window, please provide a business justification so we can escalate for a compliance exception (will likely need an SRE impact review).

Next steps I recommend:
- Samir: confirm you’re OK with sample-based fulfillment and 90-day retention (or provide rationale for a different window).
- If yes: Stephanie to produce an MSA/Order Form redline and we’ll circulate for signature.
- If no: propose a short call (we can host) to align legal/compliance expectations and list remediation commitments.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_legal_track.docx]

From: Samir Patel <samir@healthalpha.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: SOC 2 & pen-test language in Order Form

Laura / Stephanie —

On Fri, Oct 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:
> If HealthAlpha is comfortable with the sampling cadence and 90-day evidence retention, we can incorporate these clauses into the Order Form and circulate for signature.

We’re aligned with the sampling approach in principle, good tradeoff. A couple of clarifying asks before we finalize:

- Pen-test details: can Redwood provide the blackout windows (dates Redwood cannot support external testing) so we can schedule? Also confirm whether Redwood will accept redacted 3P reports as "evidence" for remediation acceptance, or whether Redwood requires the third party to deliver raw logs to Redwood for validation.
- Evidence transfer: we prefer a secure file transfer (ShareFile or SFTP) for artifact delivery. Can Redwood commit to ShareFile delivery by default, or do you require an alternative?
- Retention: our procurement team prefers a 180-day evidence retention window. If Redwood needs to keep it at 90 days we will log a compliance exception and circle back — can you confirm who owns escalation for that?

If you’re open, let’s schedule a 30-minute alignment call Monday. I’ll upload a clean PO with standard terms to HubSpot; attached is our procurement cover note.

Thanks —
Samir Patel
Director, IT Security — HealthAlpha
[Attachment: healthalpha_po_terms.pdf]
